Q: What is the first router hardening step for a new small office or home gateway?
Option1: Change default administrator credentials
Option2: Turn off Dynamic Host Configuration immediately
Option3: Disable all radios

Q: What does Internet Protocol address filtering on a small office or home router do?
Option1: Allows or blocks traffic based on source or destination Internet Protocol addresses
Option2: Moves devices to a new subnet automatically
Option3: Enables cellular failover

Q: Why apply firmware updates on a router or access point?
Option1: Patch security flaws and improve stability
Option2: Increase maximum antenna gain
Option3: Add more switch ports

Q: What is content filtering used for?
Option1: Blocking categories or sites that violate policy or are risky
Option2: Boosting signal strength
Option3: Encrypting the management page only

Q: Why does physical placement of the router matter for security?
Option1: It limits signal leakage and reduces tampering risk
Option2: It adds more Dynamic Host Configuration scope options
Option3: It creates more virtual networks automatically

Q: What is a reservation in Dynamic Host Configuration?
Option1: A mapping of a device hardware address to a fixed Internet Protocol address within the scope
Option2: A pool of public Internet addresses from the provider
Option3: A static route to another network

Q: When would a static public Internet address be used in a small office or home network?
Option1: When hosting services that need a consistent public address
Option2: When no devices use wireless
Option3: To prevent wired devices from connecting

Q: What is Universal Plug and Play on consumer routers?
Option1: Automatic port mapping and service discovery that can expose services if abused
Option2: A mode that disables encryption
Option3: A cellular data feature

Q: What is a screened subnet in a small office or home network?
Option1: A separate network segment used to isolate exposed devices such as cameras
Option2: A shielded Ethernet cable
Option3: A hidden network name on the main network
Option4: A private Internet Protocol version 6 range

Q: What does changing the wireless network name accomplish?
Option1: It removes default identifiers and helps separate networks by name
Option2: It raises encryption strength
Option3: It hides the network from all devices
Option4: It adds more channels to 2.4 GHz

Q: What is the impact of disabling broadcast of the wireless network name?
Option1: The name is not advertised but is still discoverable and provides little security benefit
Option2: The network becomes fully invisible and secure
Option3: Clients cannot connect at all

Q: Which wireless setting most directly protects confidentiality?
Option1: Use Wi-Fi Protected Access 3 or Wi-Fi Protected Access 2 with Advanced Encryption Standard
Option2: Change the channel weekly
Option3: Reduce transmit power only

Q: What is a guest network used for?
Option1: Isolating visitor traffic from the internal network
Option2: Increasing speed for known devices
Option3: Providing access to the router admin page

Q: Why might you disable guest access on a small office network?
Option1: To prevent untrusted devices from reaching any internal resources
Option2: To force devices to use 2.4 GHz only
Option3: To enable static routing
Option4: To allow Universal Plug and Play to work

Q: Why change wireless channels on the 2.4 GHz band?
Option1: To reduce co-channel and adjacent-channel interference
Option2: To increase encryption key length
Option3: To enable radar detection for all clients
Option4: To create a hidden network name

Q: What does disabling unused firewall ports do?
Option1: Reduces attack surface by preventing unwanted inbound traffic
Option2: Forces all traffic to use port 8080
Option3: Speeds up the processor by fifty percent

Q: What is port forwarding?
Option1: Mapping an external port to an internal host and port for a specific service
Option2: Blocking a port on the switch
Option3: Mirroring switch traffic for analysis
Option4: Assigning a static address via Dynamic Host Configuration

Q: A user enabled Universal Plug and Play to make a game work but security is a concern. What is the safer approach?
Option1: Manually create required port forwarding rules and leave Universal Plug and Play disabled
Option2: Turn off the firewall entirely
Option3: Enable demilitarized zone host for the entire computer
Option4: Change the network name to default

Q: Which combination best hardens a small office or home wireless network?
Option1: Strong passphrase, disable Wi-Fi Protected Setup, update firmware, and restrict admin access
Option2: Use open authentication, disable firewall, and enable Universal Plug and Play
Option3: Hide the network name and leave default password
Option4: Reduce transmit power and use Wired Equivalent Privacy

Q: How can you limit exposure of the router administration interface from the internet?
Option1: Disable remote management or restrict it to a virtual private network or specific source addresses
Option2: Enable Universal Plug and Play for admin
Option3: Open port 80 to the world
Option4: Use the same password as the wireless network

Q: Why keep router time accurate?
Option1: Because log timestamps and certificate checks rely on correct time
Option2: To improve antenna alignment
Option3: To increase Dynamic Host Configuration pool size

Q: A smart camera must be reachable from outside with minimal risk. What is the best design?
Option1: Place it in a screened subnet or guest virtual local area network and forward only needed ports
Option2: Place it on the main network with Universal Plug and Play
Option3: Expose the router admin page

Q: A small office wants to block adult sites on all clients. Which setting helps?
Option1: Enable content filtering with the desired categories or use a Domain Name System filter
Option2: Disable broadcast of the network name
Option3: Change the local network address range

Q: Which control prevents nearby users from guessing the wireless key by push button?
Option1: Disable Wi-Fi Protected Setup and use a strong passphrase
Option2: Use hidden network name only
Option3: Use open authentication

Q: How do you prevent router admin exposure to the internet?
Option1: Disable remote management or restrict it to a virtual private network or specific source addresses
Option2: Allow admin over unencrypted web from any host
Option3: Enable Universal Plug and Play for admin

Q: A device needs inbound access. What is the least exposed approach?
Option1: Single port forward to the device with a screened subnet or guest virtual local area network
Option2: Enable demilitarized zone host for the device
Option3: Turn off the firewall
